# Lesson 3: Sentinel Data

## Task 1

Download a Sentinel-2 **L2A** scene of your choice from the [Copernicus Browser](https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/) (follow the steps from the lesson slides). Extract the `.zip` archive and note the path to the resulting `.SAFE` folder.

Import the Blue (B02), Green (B03), Red (B04), and NIR (B08) bands from the `IMG_DATA/R10m/` subfolder (see [Spectral Bands (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentinel-2#Spectral_bands)). Convert digital numbers to surface reflectance using scale and offset manually.

After converting, plot a histogram of one band with `hist()` and inspect `minmax(s2)`. What do you notice about the value range, and why does this happen? Clip all values to [0, 1] using `app()` and store the result back as `s2`.

```{r}
library(terra)
library(stringr)

img_dir <- "data-large/S2B_MSIL2A_20240915T102559_N0511_R108_T32TMS_20240915T131207.SAFE/GRANULE/L2A_T32TMS_A039316_20240915T102803/IMG_DATA/R10m/"

s2_files <- list.files(img_dir, "\\.jp2$", full.names = TRUE)
s2_files <- s2_files[str_detect(s2_files, "B0[2348]")]

s2 <- rast(s2_files)
names(s2) <- str_split_fixed(names(s2), "_", 4)[, 3]

s2 <- (s2 - 1000) / 10000

# Values below 0 (dark pixels, ESA offset artefact) and above 1 (bright surfaces)
hist(s2[[1]])
minmax(s2)

force_minmax <- \(x, min = 0, max = 1) {
  x[x < min] <- min
  x[x > max] <- max
  x
}

s2 <- app(s2, force_minmax)
```

## Task 2

Visualize the Sentinel-2 image as a **True Color** composite (Red = B04, Green = B03, Blue = B02) and a **False Color** composite (Red = B08/NIR, Green = B04, Blue = B03). Use `plotRGB()` with `stretch = "histogram"`.

Which land cover types appear bright red in the False Color image, and why?

```{r}
# True Color: R=B04, G=B03, B=B02
plotRGB(s2, r = 3, g = 2, b = 1, stretch = "histogram", main = "True Color")

# False Color: R=B08(NIR), G=B04(Red), B=B03(Green)
# healthy vegetation reflects strongly in NIR → bright red
plotRGB(s2, r = 4, g = 3, b = 2, stretch = "histogram", main = "False Color (NIR)")
```

## Task 3

The SCL band is not in `R10m/` — find it in the `IMG_DATA/R20m/` folder of your SAFE archive using `list.files()` with `pattern = "SCL"`. Import it, resample to match `s2`, and apply a cloud mask keeping only pixels classified as vegetation (4), bare soils (5), water (6), or snow/ice (11).

Resample the SCL to match the resolution of `s2` before masking (use `method = "near"`). Store the result as `s2_masked` and report what percentage of pixels are cloud-free.

```{r}
scl_file <- list.files(
  "data-large/S2B_MSIL2A_20240915T102559_N0511_R108_T32TMS_20240915T131207.SAFE/GRANULE/L2A_T32TMS_A039316_20240915T102803/IMG_DATA/R20m/",
  pattern = "SCL.*\\.jp2$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
scl <- rast(scl_file)

# Resample SCL to match s2 — nearest-neighbour preserves class values
scl <- resample(scl, s2, method = "near")

valid_classes <- c(4, 5, 6, 11)
cloud_mask <- scl %in% valid_classes
s2_masked <- mask(s2, cloud_mask, maskvalues = FALSE)

n_valid <- global(!is.na(s2_masked[[1]]), sum)[[1]]
cat(sprintf("Valid pixels: %.1f%%\n", 100 * n_valid / ncell(s2_masked)))
```

## Task 4

Compute NDVI from both `s2` (unmasked) and `s2_masked` (cloud-masked):

$$\text{NDVI} = \frac{\text{B08} - \text{B04}}{\text{B08} + \text{B04}}$$

Compare the global mean NDVI of both images using `global(..., mean, na.rm = TRUE)`. Why does the masked image have a higher mean NDVI?

```{r}
ndvi        <- (s2[["B08"]] - s2[["B04"]]) / (s2[["B08"]] + s2[["B04"]])
ndvi_masked <- (s2_masked[["B08"]] - s2_masked[["B04"]]) / (s2_masked[["B08"]] + s2_masked[["B04"]])

global(ndvi,        mean, na.rm = TRUE)
global(ndvi_masked, mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Clouds reflect strongly and nearly equally across all bands → NDVI ≈ 0 or negative.
# Removing cloud pixels reveals the true surface signal.
```

## Task 5

Write the cloud-masked NDVI to disk in two ways:

a) As `Float32` (full precision, no transformation)
b) As `Byte` (0–255) using `scoff_params()` to compute scale and offset, with `DEFLATE` compression

Compare the file sizes using `file.size()`. Then read the Byte file back and compute the maximum absolute difference from the original NDVI using `global(abs(...), max, na.rm = TRUE)`. How large is the precision loss?

```{r}
dir.create("data-out", showWarnings = FALSE)

# a) Float32
writeRaster(ndvi_masked, "data-out/ndvi_float32.tif", datatype = "FLT4S", overwrite = TRUE)

# b) Byte with scoff_params
scoff_params <- function(x, a = 0, b = 255) {
  stopifnot(nlyr(x) == 1)
  mm     <- minmax(x)[, 1]
  scale  <- (b - a) / (mm[2] - mm[1])
  offset <- (a * mm[2] - b * mm[1]) / (mm[2] - mm[1])
  c(scale = 1 / scale, offset = -offset)
}

so <- scoff_params(ndvi_masked)

writeRaster(
  ndvi_masked,
  "data-out/ndvi_byte.tif",
  datatype  = "INT1U",
  scale     = so["scale"],
  offset    = so["offset"],
  gdal      = "COMPRESS=DEFLATE",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# Compare file sizes
cat(sprintf("Float32: %.0f KB\n", file.size("data-out/ndvi_float32.tif") / 1024))
cat(sprintf("Byte:    %.0f KB\n", file.size("data-out/ndvi_byte.tif")    / 1024))

# Check precision loss
ndvi_restored <- rast("data-out/ndvi_byte.tif")
global(abs(ndvi_restored - ndvi_masked), max, na.rm = TRUE)
```
